assignments.brief_reason: Uses a dangerousness/harm threshold while still valuing free speech.
Concern about extremity/actions, but not clearly mapped to threats/toxicity language removals.
Removes for factual misleading info and intentionally divisive rhetoric (toxicity/divisiveness).
Politeness increases allowance; fits the toxicity/lowers-when-uncivil pattern.
Focus on wording/framing where cussing/derogatory language reduces acceptance (toxicity filter).
Prefers fruitful/pro-social discussion over hatred/angry hostile words (keeps non-toxic content).
Focus on exposure/critical thinking and rejection of monetizing speech, not clearly the codebook’s threat/toxicity/free-speech-exceptions themes.
Removes both sides if either is inflammatory/crude, aligning with removing toxic/inflammatory content.
Removal triggered by hostile/profane/rude language (toxicity) regardless of viewpoints.
Distinguishes opinions vs hate and credits fairness from seeing both sides; primarily removal of hate aligns with toxicity removal.
Harm/disinformation drives removal even if only one side is problematic.
Explicitly removes hateful words while protecting free speech—violence-free speech exceptions.
Chooses the most reasonable to share; does not clearly map to threat/toxicity criteria.
Wants to tone down anger/inflammatoriness because it’s too inflammatory—toxicity/inflammatory language filter.
Conversation quality vs rude namecalling; removes when devolving into harassment/namecalling (toxicity).
Constructive vs hostility/harassment/incitement to violence; removal for violence-related abuse fits violence/threat exception.
Assesses hostility/foul/derogatory/exclusionist comments and applies equally across sides—removing toxic language.
Reciprocity/symmetry across mirrored pair is about equal treatment, but not clearly about applying identical moderation criteria across political viewpoints.
Evidence/objectivity vs personal attack; personal-attack removal aligns with removing toxic/harassing content.
Removes harm/violence risk and misinformation; violence/harm-based exception to keep speech.
